items.reasonDeferred: The UI exposes many additional board-family and clone-oriented labels that do not identify one electrically stable manufacturer SKU or revision. Adding ratings or pin maps from those labels alone would violate VFAI-008's exact-variant and evidence requirements.
blockingEvidence: Voltforge_UI/src/features/canvas/boardCatalog.ts contains board families beyond the eight exact variants approved in electronics_corpus v1.

Manufacturer documents, exact SKU/revision mappings, and maintained pinout evidence must be reviewed per variant; existing UI marketing labels and legacy generator tables are not sufficient provenance.
proposedWork: Inventory every remaining UI board and component type against an exact manufacturer SKU/revision or explicitly classify it variant-required/unsupported.
Add manufacturer-evidenced board, pin-map, component, wiring, firmware, diagnostic, simulation, and safety records without weakening checksum or unknown-result gates.

items.title: Add compiler-verified firmware shards for the remaining exact board variants
items.reasonDeferred: VFAI-009 can only admit firmware labels proven by a version-pinned target compiler. The first release pins the official Arduino AVR core for UNO R3, Mega 2560 Rev3, and Nano classic; installing unrelated board cores without separate version, license, checksum, FQBN, and resource review would weaken the immutable toolchain gate.
blockingEvidence: The verified release rejects firmware candidates for Arduino UNO R4 WiFi, ESP32-DevKitC V4 WROOM-32E-N4, ESP32-S3-DevKitC-1 N8, Raspberry Pi Pico, and Raspberry Pi Pico 2 with firmware-target-not-in-v1-pinned-toolchain.
Those exact boards require Renesas, Espressif, and RP2040/RP2350 target cores rather than the pinned Arduino AVR Boards 1.8.6 core.
Each added core materially expands local toolchain size and must be bound by executable/core checksums and exact FQBN compile receipts before generated code can enter training.

Record package licenses, archive and installed-tool hashes, deterministic compile commands, and offline no-write receipt validation.
Generate board-specific firmware and compiler-repair tasks, compile every unique source, rerun duplicate/leakage gates, and publish a new immutable dataset revision.

items.title: Review the pinned Windows PyTorch runtime after the native DLL regression is resolved
items.reasonDeferred: The benchmark workstation cannot safely load newer official Windows CPU wheels: Torch 2.12.1 under isolated CPython 3.12 and the pre-existing Torch 2.13.0 under CPython 3.14 both fail while initializing c10.dll. PyTorch 2.8.0+cpu under isolated CPython 3.12 is stable and passes every VFAI-011 and AI regression, so changing framework versions again during the Gen1 architecture item would add risk without model value.
blockingEvidence: Official PyTorch issue https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/166628 tracks WinError 1114 failures in newer Windows binaries and records 2.8.0 downgrade as a working mitigation.

Official advisory GHSA-63cw-57p8-fm3p affects PyTorch <=2.9.1 and is fixed in >=2.10.0; the pinned 2.8.0 runtime may therefore be used only with trusted local checkpoints and must not activate checkpoint-backed serving.
On this host, the minimum patched torch==2.10.0+cpu candidate failed 20 of 20 clean imports under isolated CPython 3.12.13 with WinError 1114 loading c10.dll.
On this host, torch==2.12.1+cpu under CPython 3.12.13 raised WinError 1114 loading torch/lib/c10.dll before any VoltForge code executed.
The global torch==2.13.0 under CPython 3.14.4 raised the same DLL error and emitted a native access-violation trace during pytest collection.
The isolated torch==2.8.0+cpu runtime imported cleanly and completed 14 focused Gen1 tests plus the 182-test AI suite.
proposedWork: After the upstream Windows issue is resolved, test the latest maintained CPU wheel in a fresh isolated environment without altering the verified Gen1 toolchain.
Run repeated clean-process import checks, the focused Gen1 suite, the full AI suite, checkpoint compatibility tests, and VFAI-004 latency/memory benchmarks.
Review security and maintenance notes, then update the Python/Torch pin and architecture manifest together only when all gates pass.
items.reviewGate: Review after the master backlog is complete, or earlier only if a PyTorch security advisory makes 2.8.0 unacceptable; promotion requires a clean upstream Windows fix and full local regression evidence.
acceptanceCriteria: The replacement runtime imports in at least 20 fresh Windows processes without WinError 1114, access violations, or DLL load-order workarounds.
Exact parameter accounting, deterministic initialization, causal masking, KV-cache equivalence, tiny overfit, and strict save/load tests remain green.
Measured CPU latency and peak memory do not materially regress without a documented quality or maintenance benefit.
The upgrade introduces no pretrained model/tokenizer asset, hosted inference provider, or external generation API.

reviewOutcome.summary: The master backlog is complete, but the upstream Windows issue remains open, both the minimum security-patched and latest official CPU candidates fail the first mandatory local gate, and the pinned runtime is affected by a checkpoint-loading security advisory. The dependency pin remains unchanged for trusted local training/testing, while the service now fails closed before loading any active checkpoint-backed neural artifact. Architecture, full-suite, checkpoint, latency, and memory comparisons were correctly not run against candidates that cannot import.

items.title: Validate Gen1 mixed-precision resume on supported CUDA hardware
items.reasonDeferred: The VFAI-004 benchmark host exposes no CUDA accelerator and its AVX2 CPU has no native AVX-512 BF16 support. VFAI-012 implements fail-closed CUDA BF16/FP16 selection, autocast, GradScaler state capture, bounded overflow recovery/rejection, and runtime-contract resume, but this hardware cannot execute the enabled-scaler branches honestly.
blockingEvidence: torch.cuda.is_available() is false in the pinned Python 3.12/PyTorch 2.8.0+cpu environment.
torch.backends.cpu.get_cpu_capability() reports AVX2 and torch.cpu._is_avx512_bf16_supported() is false.
CPU auto precision correctly selects float32 and explicit unsupported BF16/FP16 requests are covered by fail-closed tests; no accelerator result has been claimed.
proposedWork: Run controlled FP32, BF16, and FP16+GradScaler experiments on a supported local CUDA device using identical configs, packed batches, and seeds.
Force or safely synthesize a scaler-overflow case, checkpoint after recovery, and prove exact safe-point continuation including scaler growth/backoff state.
Measure throughput, peak memory, numerical stability, validation deltas, and checkpoint portability before changing the auto-precision release policy.
items.reviewGate: Review after the master backlog or when owned CUDA hardware is available; do not rent an external model service or send governed training data to a hosted provider for this validation.
acceptanceCriteria: BF16/FP16 are enabled only on hardware that explicitly reports support and all training losses/gradients remain finite under the selected policy.
Interrupted/resumed mixed-precision runs match uninterrupted safe-point state for model, optimizer, scheduler, scaler, data cursor, and all RNGs.
A measured scorecard records speed, memory, stability, and validation impact against FP32.
No governed dataset, checkpoint, tokenizer, or project context leaves owner-controlled infrastructure.

reviewOutcome.summary: This workstation still cannot execute the CUDA acceptance matrix: Windows exposes only Intel UHD Graphics 620, nvidia-smi is absent, and the pinned PyTorch runtime reports a CPU-only build with zero CUDA devices. No BF16/FP16 performance, memory, stability, validation, or portability result is inferred. The host-independent overflow path was hardened so a skipped GradScaler update restores the exact batch cursor and all RNG state, retains the backed-off scaler state, retries within a bounded limit, and records recovery evidence before any safe-point checkpoint.
implemented: Bounded mixed-precision overflow retry with an eight-attempt fail-closed ceiling.
Exact packed-data cursor plus Python, NumPy, Torch CPU, and Torch CUDA RNG restoration before retrying the same optimizer step.
Per-step overflow retry and GradScaler before/after scale metrics.
Content-free owned-CUDA capability evaluator with BF16/FP16 arithmetic smokes and checksum-verified unmeasured states.
verification: Pinned runtime capability: torch 2.8.0+cpu, cudaAvailable=false, cudaDeviceCount=0, torchCudaBuild=null.

Creating a nominal 2,048- or 4,096-ID model vocabulary without first training and approving the corresponding project-owned tokenizer would either invent unreachable IDs or change tokenization, packing, and dataset lineage, so it cannot be an honest controlled candidate.
blockingEvidence: Tokenizer v1.1.0 is the only current approved candidate: 3,072 IDs, 2,800 merges, a fixed 16-token special-ID contract, and checksum-bound v1.1.0 corpus lineage. No approved 2,048- or 4,096-ID artifact exists.

High-volume generation remains unsafe until immutable release retention, scalable semantic deduplication, independent held-out growth, uncertainty/manual-audit evidence, and finite owner-approved storage/compute budgets exist; third-party model corpora and private user projects remain prohibited by default.

gen1_optimization/benchmark.py explicitly loads checkpoints on device=cpu, applies optimization against torch.device(cpu), and leaves validation and generation tensors on CPU; its checksum-bound historical report must not be rewritten as accelerator evidence.

items.title: Harden clean-host compiler provisioning and reusable offline verification caches
items.reasonDeferred: All five installed compiler profiles and the retained 88-receipt release verify on this workstation, but the local downloads are not a complete portable provisioning closure: only 9 of 10 manifest-declared archives match, the Arduino CLI archive and package indexes are not manifest-bound, the Pico source fallback is not a checksum-bound portable bundle, and complete host dependency, license, source, budget, clean-host, and offline-restore evidence does not exist. Provisioning or exporting the 2.67 GB observed download cache without owner-approved storage, bandwidth, time, host, and retention budgets would exceed the review gate.
blockingEvidence: Arduino-Pico 6.0.0 package extraction stalled twice; the accepted profile uses commit 0bcd162ad6c9173544cc37c6a1b63de19239e359 plus pinned recursive submodules.
The measured ESP32 probe required 353.61 seconds for a cold source and 125.66 seconds for the next source before installed caches were warm.
The current toolchain directories are local workstation state; package/source hashes are recorded, but a clean isolated host has not yet reproduced all 88 receipts.
proposedWork: Create a fail-closed provisioning script for all five profiles with checksum/license verification, resumable downloads, the documented Pico source fallback, disk budgets, and post-install identity checks.
Define content-addressed compiler/core cache exports whose keys include the complete profile, FQBN, host, CLI command, and dependency hashes; reject partial or stale caches.
Run clean-host and cache-restore verification that reproduces all 88 receipts with compilation network access disabled and records time/disk evidence.
items.reviewGate: Review before moving compiler verification to CI or another workstation; approve explicit storage, bandwidth, clean-host, and cache-retention budgets.
acceptanceCriteria: A clean supported Windows host provisions every profile from checksummed inputs and reproduces all exact receipts.
Offline compilation succeeds after provisioning, and missing, corrupt, partial, or mismatched caches fail closed.
Warm verification time and disk use meet declared budgets without weakening per-source or per-FQBN evidence.
Provisioning adds compiler dependencies only and no external AI model or inference service.

reviewOutcome.summary: No host was provisioned and no cache was exported. FU-014 is accepted for later with a fail-closed readiness contract: the evaluator confirms the current installed identities and retained compiler receipts, records the local cache only as non-portable observation evidence, and blocks all later work until a complete checksummed input closure and explicit owner budget exist.
implemented: Frozen the five-profile, 11-FQBN, 88-receipt Windows scope, exact Arduino CLI compile-command contract, offline-after-provisioning boundary, and explicit no-mutation rules.

Added a content-addressed per-profile cache-key contract binding the toolchain manifest, profile/core/version, all FQBNs, host, CLI identity and command, package-index hashes, dependency archives, and source/submodule identity.
Added exact cache inventory verification that rejects missing, extra, changed, duplicated, path-escaping, noncanonical, or stale-key content.
Added a checksum-bound sequential readiness evaluator with semantic input-closure, owner-budget, five-profile cache-export, clean-host, offline-restore, and independent-review gates.
Added deterministic FU-014 regression coverage to the fast cross-repository AI contract.
verification: Current source and installed identity evidence passes for all 5 profiles and 11 exact FQBNs.
The retained compiler release passes with 88 receipts: 66 successful compilations and 22 intentional expected failures; no fresh compilation was performed by the readiness evaluator.

The local downloads observation contains 47 files and 2,665,518,001 bytes; 9 of 10 manifest-declared archives match, while xtensa-esp-elf-14.2.0_20260121-i686-w64-mingw32.zip is absent by exact declared name.
The Arduino CLI archive, both package indexes, and Pico fallback bundle are not yet bound as a complete portable provisioning input closure; no cache export is configured.

Readiness evaluate and stale-check verification pass with decision complete-checksummed-provisioning-input-closure and zero downloads, exports, provisions, compiler runs, receipt rewrites, or synthetic-data mutations.
Focused FU-014 regression: 13 passed.
Full AI regression: 531 passed, 5 skipped, 5 subtests passed.
unmeasured: Owner-approved download, installed-byte, retained-cache, provisioning-time, clean-host-time, and cache-retention budgets
Clean supported Windows host provisioning from a complete checksummed dependency closure
Offline reproduction of all 88 receipts after provisioning and after cache restore
Missing, partial, corrupt, extra, stale, host-mismatched, FQBN-mismatched, and command-mismatched cache behavior on the approved clean host
Warm verification time, total installed disk use, cache export size, restoration time, bandwidth, and retention cost
reviewOutcome.nextReviewGate: First complete and independently review a license/source/checksum-bound provisioning-input manifest for the CLI, package indexes, every host dependency, and the Pico fallback bundle. Then obtain explicit owner storage, bandwidth, host, time, and retention budgets before downloading, exporting a cache, or provisioning a clean host.

items.title: Preserve immutable versioned synthetic releases and repair historical tokenizer lineage retention
items.reasonDeferred: Write-once content-addressed retention is now enforced and tokenizer v1.1.0 resolves to exact retained bytes without rewriting its approved manifest. FU-015 cannot complete because no owner-approved encrypted external-backup/retention policy, independent backup receipt, or restore receipt exists. Tokenizer v1.0.0 remains explicitly non-reconstructable from retained trusted bytes: none of its four exact historical shard hashes is available, so current data cannot substitute for that history.
blockingEvidence: The v1.0.0 tokenizer manifest declares four 154-record shard hashes that differ from the current 250-record release at the same paths.
A workspace search found no retained JSONL files with the four historical SHA-256 values, and Git HEAD versions do not match them.
Current training is safely moved to tokenizer v1.1.0, while historical bootstrap execution fails closed rather than substituting current data.
proposedWork: Publish future synthetic releases under immutable revision/content-addressed directories and make every tokenizer/model manifest reference those paths rather than a mutable current alias.
Search trusted owner backups for the exact v1.0.0 shard bytes; if recovered, verify all declared hashes and archive them without changing the historical tokenizer manifest.
If recovery is impossible, retain an explicit reproducibility limitation on historical artifacts and prevent any release process from claiming full data reconstruction.
items.reviewGate: Review before the next tokenizer or model training revision; immutable release retention and backup policy must be approved before new training starts.
acceptanceCriteria: Every new tokenizer/model lineage resolves to immutable retained shard bytes and manifests whose checksums remain valid after later releases.
Current aliases may move, but immutable version paths cannot be overwritten and deletion impact is fail-closed.
Historical v1.0.0 lineage is either exactly restored from trusted bytes or clearly classified as non-reconstructable without rewriting evidence.
Backup/restore and source-removal checks cover all retained release revisions.

reviewOutcome.summary: FU-015 is accepted for later after implementing repository-side immutable retention. Two write-once releases preserve the pre-change tokenizer v1.1.0 lineage and the current pipeline 1.3.0 release; current training resolves the approved tokenizer's exact existing shard and manifest identities to retained bytes without modifying that tokenizer. Completion remains blocked on owner-approved external retention, backup, and independent restore evidence.
implemented: Published content-addressed synthetic releases with exact mirrored paths, byte counts, SHA-256 identities, self-checksummed manifests, exact inventories, and a separately checksummed mutable CURRENT pointer.

Changed pipeline revision 1.3.0 to preserve the prior current payload before lock/output mutation, refuse in-place repair or overwrite, publish the new release, and require current-pointer verification before release checks pass.

Retained tokenizer v1.1.0 byte-for-byte and changed Gen1 training resolution to validate its declared shard identities against immutable release bytes, snapshotted governance, source origins, producer lock, leakage gate, and task schema.
Changed the tokenizer no-write check to retrain against retained immutable lineage and reject CLI overwrite of an approved tokenizer release.
Extended source-removal analysis to include every retained immutable manifest while keeping impact reports non-authorizing.

Added a sequential readiness contract for historical classification, owner backup policy, external backup, restore, and independent review plus deterministic tamper, restore, and non-overwrite regression coverage.
verification: Retained 2 immutable releases with 52 exact files and 2,882,599 total bytes; current pointer resolves to pipeline 1.3.0 release vf-synthetic-1.3.0-e90691f629808e1478d8.
Tokenizer v1.1.0 resolves all 4 declared shards to retained release vf-synthetic-1.2.0-1594f89c93854f971d3a and its deterministic no-write retrain check passes without rewriting tokenizer files.

Tokenizer v1.0.0 declares 4 shards and 154 records; 26 retained/workspace JSONL files were hashed and none matched its four historical SHA-256 identities, so it is classified non-reconstructable-from-retained-trusted-bytes.
Both governed source-removal reports include all 8 retained shard-manifest instances across both immutable releases and do not authorize deletion.
Synthetic release verification passes with 251 candidates, 250 accepted records, one duplicate rejection, zero held-out collisions, and all 88 retained compiler receipts unchanged.
Focused immutable retention, readiness, governance, Gen1 loader, and tokenizer regression: 41 passed.
Full AI regression: 543 passed, 5 skipped, 5 subtests passed.
unmeasured: Owner-approved retention days, minimum independent copies, maximum backup bytes, maximum restore time, storage owner, encryption, access-control, and checksum policy
External backup creation and object inventory for every retained release
Independent restoration from external storage, measured restore duration, and post-restore source-removal impact verification
Trusted owner-backup recovery of tokenizer v1.0.0's four exact historical shard byte sequences
reviewOutcome.nextReviewGate: Supply a checksum-bound owner backup/retention policy with finite storage and restore limits. Then back up every retained release to the approved encrypted boundary, restore all releases independently, verify exact inventories and source-removal impact, and submit both receipts for independent review; do not rewrite v1.0.0 history or treat repository retention as an external backup.
